evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this will just take like, you know, ten minutes to provide you an accurate estimate. Is that okay?' — mentions time frame and no explicit promise of a dependable quote; does not wait for full confirmation before pivoting to discovery.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Jacob), moving day (Sunday November 1st), origin (3623 West Alabama Street, 4th floor), destination (500 Crawford Street, 7th floor), apartment type (one bedroom) — all four elements confirmed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment, 4th to 7th floor), elevator access (confirmed at both ends), walking distances (pickup to elevator, elevator to door), rooms (one bedroom confirmed), furniture inventory (couch with chase, chair, coffee table, entertainment center, bed frame, bar/shelf, ~20 boxes), special items (55-inch TV, two pieces of art later clarified as not super valuable), no washer/dryer, no piano/safe/workout equipment. Covers property type, floors, rooms, walking distances, additional items, and special considerations.
evidence_quotes.packing_services: Not offered. Rep never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count: Customer volunteers 'around like twenty boxes' unprompted, but rep does not ask the rubric version ('typical box count for a home your size is X, do you have anything like china or a book collection that might put you over').
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep states: 'typical one bedroom apartment usually takes two movers, one truck between two and a half to three and a half hours to completely move. In your case... I would estimate your move to be around four and a half hours' and 'it's safe to budget around $864 for four and a half hours.' Personalizes to fourth-floor-to-seventh-floor with elevator access and walking distances, providing both range and personalization.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep covers hourly rate ($192/hour for two movers), what's included (fuel, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, blankets, tools), no hidden fees explicitly stated, and time-clock mechanics: 'the time starts as soon as we get on site and open the contract... two and a half hour minimum and once we go over that minimum, the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.' Covers fee transparency and the 2.5-hour-minimum/15-minute-increments framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_silence: After estimate is given, rep asks 'Do you have questions or clarification on that?' — not the rubric version 'Does that feel fair?' No explicit pause/silence follows; customer simply responds 'No, that seems pretty straightforward.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Rep delivers: 'we have our on time guarantee. So we value your time if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and all of that is included at no extra cost.' Covers discount terms and immediate discounting on lateness.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage: Rep states: 'We provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages. Unlike our competitors who either charge extra or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage.' Mentions $2,000 and no-deductible framing; does not explicitly state 'built into the rate, not an add-on,' though it is grouped in the 'no extra cost' statement.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. After delivering both promises together, transitions directly to time-clock explanation with no confirming close.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns: Rep never asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?' After estimate discussion, moves straight to explicit ask without a final genuine concerns check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all: Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks 'would you like our help with your move on Sunday November 1st?' — plainly framed without softening. However, customer responds 'If you could send me the quote and I'll review it and then I will confirm at a later date' and rep accepts: 'I'll go ahead and send it to your email.' This gives an easy out (email review instead of verbal commitment).
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: Not mentioned. Rep does not reference rate holding or lock-in terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirms: email address (Jacob.Rodriguez.2206@gmail.com), date (Sunday November 1st), and sending quote via email. Does NOT confirm: phone number, arrival window, crew size, destination address (mentioned but not re-confirmed as a booking detail), or notes for the crew about customer concerns. Partial confirmation (2 of 5+ items).

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, floors, walking distances, full furniture inventory, special items) efficiently and personalized the estimate thoughtfully to the customer's specific floor-to-floor situation.
coaching_note: Rep skipped the entire Section 2 (Their Agenda + Two Layers Deep + Active Listening) — jumped straight from introductory time-frame into logistics probing without ever asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' and never circled back to concerns before closing; combine with missing Section 6 concerns-again check and no final silence after the estimate to create a transactional feel that invited the easy out at the ask.
